title: Out of cat food
setting: A rainy weeknight at the office, just after eight. Everyone else has gone home. Yuki is about to leave, but her coworker Mai, who lives with her cat, is still at her desk.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mai, mada kaeranai no? mou hachiji da yo.
lines.ja: マイ、まだ帰らないの？もう八時だよ。
lines.kana: まい、まだかえらないの？もうはちじだよ。
lines.english: Mai, aren't you going home yet? It's already eight.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un, mou chotto. kyou mo kaeri osoku naru naa.
lines.ja: うん、もうちょっと。今日も帰り遅くなるなあ。
lines.kana: うん、もうちょっと。きょうもかえりおそくなるなあ。
lines.english: Yeah, a bit longer. Looks like I'll be home late again today.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: neko-chan, daijoubu? kaeri ga osoi to, okoranai?
lines.ja: 猫ちゃん、大丈夫？帰りが遅いと、怒らない？
lines.kana: ねこちゃん、だいじょうぶ？かえりがおそいと、おこらない？
lines.english: What about your cat? Doesn't she get cross when you're home late?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: okoru yo. uchi ni kaettara, zutto naiteru no.
lines.ja: 怒るよ。うちに帰ったら、ずっと鳴いてるの。
lines.kana: おこるよ。うちにかえったら、ずっとないてるの。
lines.english: She does. When I get home, she meows at me nonstop.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kyou, nanji ni uchi deta no?
lines.ja: 今日、何時にうち出たの？
lines.kana: きょう、なんじにうちでたの？
lines.english: What time did you leave the house today?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: rokuji han ni uchi o dete, sore kara zutto koko.
lines.ja: 六時半にうちを出て、それからずっとここ。
lines.kana: ろくじはんにうちをでて、それからずっとここ。
lines.english: I left the house at six thirty, and I've been here ever since.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, soto ni mo detenai no?
lines.kana: え、そとにもでてないの？
lines.english: What, you haven't even stepped outside?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.ja: 出てないよ。お腹もすいた。
lines.kana: でてないよ。おなかもすいた。

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jaa, chotto soto ni deyou yo. ame mo yanda shi.
lines.ja: じゃあ、ちょっと外に出ようよ。雨もやんだし。
lines.kana: じゃあ、ちょっとそとにでようよ。あめもやんだし。
lines.english: Then let's step out for a bit. The rain's stopped, anyway.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: soto ka. a! kyou, kaimono ni ikanai to. neko no gohan, mou nai n da.
lines.ja: 外か。あ！今日、買い物に行かないと。猫のごはん、もうないんだ。
lines.kana: そとか。あ！きょう、かいものにいかないと。ねこのごはん、もうないんだ。
lines.english: Outside, huh. Oh! I have to go shopping today. I'm out of cat food.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mou kaerina yo. sore wa ashita!
lines.ja: もう帰りなよ。それは明日！
lines.kana: もうかえりなよ。それはあした！
lines.english: Just go home already. That can wait till tomorrow!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un, kyou wa mou uchi ni kaeru!
lines.ja: うん、今日はもううちに帰る！
lines.kana: うん、きょうはもううちにかえる！

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kaimono, watashi mo iku yo. de, mai no uchi ni mo itte ii?
lines.ja: 買い物、私も行くよ。で、マイのうちにも行っていい？
lines.kana: かいもの、わたしもいくよ。で、まいのうちにもいっていい？
lines.english: I'll come shopping with you. And can I come over to your place too?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: ii yo! kyou wa kaeri osoku naranai shi, neko-chan mo okoranai ne.
lines.ja: いいよ！今日は帰り遅くならないし、猫ちゃんも怒らないね。
lines.kana: いいよ！きょうはかえりおそくならないし、ねこちゃんもおこらないね。
lines.english: Sure! I won't be home late today, and she won't be cross either.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.ja: やった！じゃあ、買い物行こう！
lines.kana: やった！じゃあ、かいものいこう！

choices.english: Mai stays to finish her work, so Yuki goes to buy the cat food and drops it off at Mai's place.
Yuki and Mai step out for a quick bite to eat, then Mai comes back to finish her work.
Mai remembers she's out of cat food, so she goes home now instead of staying late. Yuki goes shopping with her and will come over to her place.

questions.explanation: Line 2: Mai expects to be home late again (kyou mo kaeri osoku naru naa). Line 9: Yuki suggests stepping out (chotto soto ni deyou yo), which reminds Mai that she has to go shopping because she's out of cat food (line 10: kaimono ni ikanai to. neko no gohan, mou nai n da). Yuki tells her to go home and leave the work till tomorrow (line 11: mou kaerina yo. sore wa ashita!), Mai agrees (line 12: kyou wa mou uchi ni kaeru!), and Yuki says she'll come shopping too and asks to come over (line 13). A is wrong: Mai doesn't stay, and Yuki goes shopping with her, not for her (kaimono, watashi mo iku yo). B is wrong: they never step out for food and come back. The work waits till tomorrow (line 11), and Mai goes home.

questions.english: Your friend Mai sees you packing up at the end of the day and asks, "are, ima kara doko iku no?" (Oh, where are you off to now?) Tell her you're going home.
questions.ja: あれ、今からどこ行くの？
questions.kana: あれ、いまからどこいくの？
questions.romaji: are, ima kara doko iku no?
questions.answer: Say you're going home with kaeru, even though she asked with iku: uchi ni kaeru yo.
questions.explanation: Mai asked with iku (doko iku no?), but going back to your own home is kaeru: uchi ni kaeru. uchi ni iku would mean going to someone else's place. In the scene, Mai says she's going home in line 12 (kyou wa mou uchi ni kaeru!), and in the very next line Yuki asks to visit Mai's place with iku (line 13: mai no uchi ni mo itte ii?). Yuki's line 1 (mada kaeranai no?) is the same kaeru with uchi ni left out. The second model is the polite version, for someone like Tanaka-san.

questions.english: Yuki asks Mai what time she left the house today. How does Mai answer?
questions.ja: マイさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: I left home for good at six thirty, and I've been here ever since.
choices.romaji: rokuji han ni uchi o hanarete, sore kara zutto koko.

choices.english: I left the house at six thirty, and I've been here ever since.
choices.romaji: rokuji han ni uchi o dete, sore kara zutto koko.

choices.english: At six thirty I came out to the house, and I've been here ever since.
choices.romaji: rokuji han ni uchi ni dete, sore kara zutto koko.

questions.explanation: Line 6: Mai says rokuji han ni uchi o dete. Setting off from home for the day is deru, and the place you leave takes o. Yuki's question in line 5 is the same phrase with o dropped (nanji ni uchi deta no?). C swaps in ni, the particle for where you end up (soto ni deru, uchi ni kaeru), so it would mean coming out to the house. A is English 'leave' turned into hanareru: uchi o hanareru is leaving home to live somewhere else, not heading out for the day.

questions.english: When Mai says she hasn't even been outside, Yuki says "jaa, chotto soto ni deyou yo." What is she suggesting?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、どうしたいですか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、どうしたいですか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, dou shitai desu ka?

choices.english: That they step out of the building for a little while.
That they both stop work and go home for the night.
That they go out for an evening of drinks together.

questions.explanation: Line 9: soto ni deru is getting out of the building, and chotto makes it just for a bit. Yuki says it right after Mai admits she hasn't stepped outside all day (line 7: soto ni mo detenai no? / line 8: detenai yo), and adds that the rain has stopped (ame mo yanda shi). B is wrong: going home is kaeru, which Yuki only says later, in line 11 (mou kaerina yo), once Mai remembers the cat food. C reads it as English 'go out' for an evening out. soto ni deru only means stepping outside, and chotto keeps it short.

questions.english: You're at home with Yuki. You pick up your bag and head for the door, and she asks, "are, deru no?" (Oh, are you going out?) Tell her you're popping out to do some shopping.
questions.answer: Say you're going shopping, with kaimono straight before (ni) iku: un, chotto kaimono itte kuru.

modelAnswers.ja: うん、ちょっと買い物行ってくる。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'm just popping out to the shops.

questions.explanation: kaimono (shopping) goes straight before ni iku. kaimono suru ni iku is the mistake; with the verb it would be kaimono shi ni iku. Mai says it in line 10 (kaimono ni ikanai to, I have to go shopping), and Yuki in lines 13 and 15 (kaimono, watashi mo iku yo / kaimono ikou!). itte kuru (go and come back) is the usual way to say you're popping out and will be back; the second model just says where you're going. kaimono covers any buying errand, cat food and groceries included.

questions.english: You share a flat with Yuki. As you leave in the morning, she asks, "kyou, nanji ni kaeru?" (What time will you be home today?) You've got a lot of work on. Tell her you'll be home late.
questions.kana: きょう、なんじにかえる？
questions.answer: Say your getting home will be late, with kaeri and osoku naru: kyou wa kaeri osoku naru.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, kyou wa kaeri osoku naru.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、今日は帰り遅くなる。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I'll be home late today.

modelAnswers.ja: 今日、帰り遅くなるから。
modelAnswers.english: Just so you know, I'll be home late today.

questions.explanation: Getting home late is kaeri ga osoi. For your own heads-up about tonight it becomes osoku naru (will get late), usually with ga dropped. Mai says it in line 2 (kyou mo kaeri osoku naru naa), and line 14 is the happy opposite (kyou wa kaeri osoku naranai). Ending with kara, as in the second model, makes it a heads-up: so don't wait for me. Not okureru: that's being late for something with a set time, like a train or a meeting.

newWords.english: cat (neko-chan: a fond way to say 'the cat')
food, a meal (neko no gohan = cat food)
leave, move away from (a place, to live elsewhere)
yay! (past of yaru, used as a cheer)
